texts.facts: The petitioner has filed the present petition like Public - : 2 :- Interest Litigation seeking implementation of provision Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in the State of Madhya Pradesh especially mainly in respect of establishment of Food Testing Laboratories at Indore, Jabalpur, Ujjain and Gwalior and tools to Food safety officer for preliminary examination for the food articles in case of food adulteration. 2. According to the petitioner, he is a socially active person and Ex- Corporator of Municipal Corporation. He had filed a PIL raising issue in respect of the construction of '' Treasure Island'' and ''Noise Pollution'', therefore, he may kindly be permitted to file a petition in the nature of PIL. The relevant part of the reply submitted by respondent no. 1 is as under: ''9.
texts.arguments: Looking at his public-spirited antecedent and the nature of the issue raised by him we are deciding this Public Interest Litigation on merit. 3. According to the petitioner, the Government of India has enacted the law in the name of "the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006" ( in short Act of 2006) to check the standard of the food and to ensure the safety of human life. Under the provision of the aforesaid Act, Manufacturing, storage, distribution, sale and import of the food articles are liable to be examined by officers and employees appointed by the appropriate Government from time to time under the Act, 2006. The Act of 2006 provides the establishment of different authorities at Central, State, also local areas for effective implementation of the provision of the Act. - : 3 :- Under the aforesaid Act of 2006, the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India has been established under Section 4 of the Act which is the parent body and has control over the overall functioning and enforcement of the Act, 2006. In addition to the above, there is also a provision of the establishment of State Food Safety Authority in each State headed by ''Designated Officer'' and '' Food Safety Officer'' at local levels. Both the officers are having power under the Act of 2006 to take samples of food for testing, seize any food article, prohibit the sale of unauthorized food and filing of a criminal case before the competent Court. According to the petitioner, the chapter 8 deals with the procedure for the '' Analysis of Food'' and Chapter 9 provides deals with the '' Offences and Penalties'' on contravention of the provision of the Act of 2006. According to the petitioner in the State of Madhya Pradesh three Food Testing Laboratories at Bhopal, Indore and Ujjain are sanctioned for scientific analysis and to check the standards of different food articles of the food articles but out of three, only one laboratory is functioning at Bhopal and the rest at Ujjain and Indore have not even constructed. The petitioner has obtained information under the Right to Information Act, 2005 that around 50% of samples were not found up to the mark and failed to satisfy the standards for want of a sufficient number of Food - : 4 :- Testing Laboratories in the State of Madhya Pradesh. One laboratory of Bhopal is not able to handle the entire burden of the State in respect of checking the standards of seized or suspicious food articles. The seized food articles are required to be checked within a reasonable time before the expiry of the shelf period. Since there is a delay in testing, therefore, the offender gets the benefit of acquittal. Hence, present petition before this Court seeking direction to the respondents to provide tools to the Food Safety Officers for on the spot analysis of the food article and also direction to the respondents to make available Food Testing Laboratories at Indore and Ujjain as functional and provide the Food Testing Laboratories in at every District and Division of State of Madhya Pradesh to ensure the food safety and standards with adequate staff. 5. Respondent No.1 has filed a reply without disputing the provision of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the Rules as described by the petitioner in the writ petition. It is further submitted that a scheme for strengthening the food safety norms has been approved by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the same is being implemented throughout the country. The aforesaid schemes include the Capacity Building of Food Testing Laboratories including support for NABL accreditation of the State Food Testing Laboratories. It is further - : 5 :- submitted that under the aforesaid scheme there is provision for the establishment of Mobile Food Testing Laboratories, for every State and Union Territory, one for every 20 districts in the State, with at least one lab in each State/Union Territory. 6. It is further submitted by respondent no. 1 that the State of - : 6 :- Madhya Pradesh has to ensure that there is a sufficient number of Food Testing Laboratories for analysis of the food products at different parts of the state and answering respondent has the limited role of granting funds under the scheme to the State of Madhya Pradesh.
